content:
marta: Quick sync — retention defaults are changing to 90 days across most SIEM indices. We need an operational playbook for when triage or IR requires longer exports (120-365d). Goal: repeatable, auditable, minimal human overhead.

jeff: Agreed. Problems we hit: random Slack asks for unwrapped logs, missing export justification, and no auto-expiry on temporary access.

saria: Proposal: create a single request endpoint (jira ticket) that kicks off an automated flow: 1) initial approver (sec-oncall) gate for up to 30d, 2) seclead for up to 180d, 3) CISO/legal if >180d or PD. Approvals generate signed audit records.

infra-bot: Reminder: KMS unwrap uses JIT-proxy. Policy currently refuses unwraps older than 90d without manual override.

marta: We should avoid manual KMS overrides. Instead: require pre-export snapshot with a signed hash before unwrap. Store snapshot in encrypted archive with its own CMK and short TTL.

jeff: For RBAC: create a time-limited role "temp/siem-exporter" with tags: "purpose", "expires_at", and an allow-list of indices. sts:AssumeRole allowed only if request has a matching ticket id tag. Session duration forced to <=12h.

saria: Ticket template idea (to be used by engineers/security):
```
- requester: <email>
- incident_or_ticket: <INC-1234>
- justification: short description of why extra window needed
- data_filters: index names, fields, time range
- sensitivity: PII/Y/N; regions affected
- kms_cmk_snapshot: <optional> (backup CMK arn)
- requested_duration_days: <int>
- masking_plan: describe fields to redact or pseudonymize
- approver_notes: 
```

legal: Add: if PII present and EU residency, include DPIA pointer and data minimization statement. Include retention justification for auditors.

sec-oncall: I can fast-approve low-risk 7-30d requests during working hours. Require a checklist: minimal query, minimal principal set, export encryption in transit+at-rest, and auto-delete scheduled. Post the approval as an event to the central audit stream.

jeff: Automation pieces: once ticket approved -> create temporary s3 export bucket with lifecycle rule `expire_after` set to the approved auto-delete date, spin up an export job that writes to that bucket, tag bucket and objects with ticket id. When job finishes, push audit event: {ticket, start_ts, end_ts, unwrapped_key_id, hash}.

infra-bot: Automation note: Block exports >50GB without seclead approval and create an alert. Also, deny any extension requests from the original requester; must open a new ticket which triggers re-eval.

marta: Edge case: KMS CMK rotates during an active retention grant. Policy: require export snapshot before rotation OR record wrapped key version IDs and ensure unwrap path in HSM for that period. Ops to document fallback.

saria: We should standardize redaction levels: NONE (raw), PARTIAL (hash/pseudonymize fields), MASKED (remove sensitive fields). Default to PARTIAL unless raw is justified.

legal: Also include a clause for subpoenas/Government requests — if there's a legal hold, auto-delete must be paused and legal must be notified.

sec-oncall: Add severity gating: for any vuln triage tied to "critical" CVSS >=9 or active exploit, escalate to seclead; cannot be auto-approved by oncall for >30d.

jeff: Implementation owners: eng-iam for role/policy, infra for export automation and bucket lifecycle, security for approval rules and audit stream, legal for DPIA and holds. We should have a short runbook and a one-pager for SRE/oncall.

marta: I'll draft the playbook and the exact ticket schema in the security docs repo under playbooks/exports-temporary-access.md, pinging owners. Draft out by EOD tomorrow.

saria: I'll prototype the Jira webhook that tags assume-role calls with ticket id so eng-iam can consume it.

infra-bot: Created placeholder task: SEC-AUTOMATION-9001 - prototype export flow (owner: jeff).

marta: Thanks everyone. Follow-ups: jeff -> infra automation; saria -> ticket webhook; eng-iam -> policy review; legal -> DPIA checklist. We'll reconvene after first draft. :spiral_calendar:
